learning_objectives.objective_text: Students restate the meaning of a fractional unit, the numerator and the denominator, mixed numbers, equivalent fractions and lowest terms, and Brahmagupta's method for adding and subtracting.

objectives.objective_text: Students find each child's share when one roti is shared equally among 2 and among 4 children, write the shares as 1/2 and 1/4, and say which share is more.
Students define a fractional unit, compare unit fractions such as 1/5 and 1/9 by thinking of shares, and collect the words for fractions used in their own languages.
Students share one whole equally on the tool, name each share as a fractional unit, and pick the bigger of two shares of the same whole.

Students find what fraction of a chikki each of two pieces is, by seeing how many copies of the small piece fill the whole, and explain why equal-sized pieces of different shapes are the same fraction.
Students name a piece as 1/n by counting how many equal pieces of that size make the whole chikki, and check the count with the small squares.
Students lay copies of a chikki piece across the whole on the tool and name each piece as a fractional unit, including triangles and L-shapes.
Students fold a unit strip into 2, 4 and 8 equal parts, name each part, and write the lengths of several parts together as multiples of the unit, such as 3 × 1/8 = 3/8.
Students write repeated halves as addition statements, read a fraction such as 3/4 as 3 × 1/4, and name the numerator and the denominator.
Students fold a strip into equal parts on the tool, lay copies of one part from the left, and write the length as k × 1/n = k/n, including lengths past one whole.
Students find the length of a line from 0 when the unit is divided into 2 or 3 equal parts, by counting the equal gaps it covers.
Students write the fractions for the marks when a unit is divided into 5 and into 8 equal parts, and see that the last mark is n/n, which is 1.
Students cut the unit into equal gaps on the tool, hop from 0 to mark fractions, and read the length of lines that end before or after 1.
Students classify fractions as less than or more than 1 unit, state the numerator and denominator pattern, and find how many whole units 3/2 and 5/2 contain.
Students write a fraction greater than 1 as a whole part plus a fractional part, read and write it as a mixed number, and turn a mixed number back into a fraction by counting units.
Students hop fractional units past 1 on the tool, group them into wholes, and convert between fractions and mixed numbers both ways.
Students compare folded strips and rows of equal wholes cut into different units to decide whether two fractions are the same length, and count how many smaller units make a larger one.

Students write division, addition and multiplication facts for a sharing situation, and show that groups with twice the units and twice the children get the same share, so 2/5 = 4/10 and 1/2 = 2/4 = 3/6.
Students list fractions equivalent to 1/2 and 2/3, notice that the numerator and the denominator are multiplied by the same number, and name the simplest form.
Students shade lengths on rows of equal wholes to test whether two fractions are equivalent, and fill in missing numbers in equivalent fractions.
Students test whether a fraction is in lowest terms, reduce 16/20 and 36/60 in steps and in one go, and explain why both ways give the same answer.
Students divide the numerator and the denominator by common factors on the tool until the fraction is in lowest terms.
Students decide which group's children get more chikki by writing 1/2 as 4/8, and explain why more units among the same children, or the same units among fewer children, gives a bigger share.
Students compare fractions such as 3/4 and 7/10, 4/5 and 7/9, by writing equivalent fractions with a common denominator, and state the two steps of comparing.
Students re-cut two fractions into a common unit on the tool, compare them, and put sets of fractions in ascending and descending order.
Students add fractions with the same denominator using strips and the number line, by counting the fractional units, and write a sum greater than 1 as a mixed number.
Students add fractions with different denominators by rewriting them with a common multiple of the denominators, adding the numerators, and giving the answer in lowest terms.
Students re-cut fraction bars into a common unit on the tool, slide the units together, and write the sum in lowest terms or as a mixed number.
Students subtract fractions with the same denominator by removing units on a strip and by jumping back on the number line.
Students subtract fractions with different denominators by converting both to a common unit, and explain why 3/4 is multiplied by 3/3 and 2/3 by 4/4.
Students re-cut fraction bars into a common unit on the tool, take away units, and write the difference in lowest terms, including word problems about distance and time.
Students name the old Indian words for fraction, describe the Indian way of writing fractions, and state Brahmagupta's rule for adding and subtracting.
Students fill a circle with different fractional units on the tool to find three and four different unit fractions that add up to 1.
Students restate the meaning of a fractional unit, the numerator and the denominator, mixed numbers, equivalent fractions and lowest terms, and Brahmagupta's method for adding and subtracting.

video_coverage.book_item: Book item: If one roti is divided equally between two children, how much roti will each child get? If one roti is shared equally among 4 children, how much will one child get? Which is more, 1/2 roti or 1/4 roti?

Book item: Find out and discuss the words for fractions that are used in the different languages spoken in your home, city, or state. Ask your grandparents, parents, teachers, and classmates what words they use for different fractions, such as for one and a half, three quarters, one and a quarter, half, quarter, and two and a half, and write them.

Book item: Fill in the blank with a fraction: A wholesale merchant packed 1 kg of rice in four packets of equal weight. The weight of each packet is ___ kg.
Book item: Fill in the blank with a fraction: Four friends ordered 3 glasses of sugarcane juice and shared it equally among themselves. Each one drank ____ glass of sugarcane juice.
Book item: Fill in the blank with a fraction: The big fish weighs 1/2 kg. The small one weighs 1/4 kg. Together they weigh ____ kg.
Book item: Arrange these fraction words in order of size from the smallest to the biggest: One and a half, three quarters, one and a quarter, half, quarter, two and a half.

We get 1/6 chikki pieces of different shapes. Are they of the same size?

Book item: A whole chikki (6 squares across, 4 down) is split by 2 vertical lines into 3 equal strips. One strip, 2 squares across and 4 squares down, is shown. What is the fractional unit of chikki shown?

Book item: The pieces below are different fractional units of a whole chikki. The whole chikki is a rectangle of 24 equal small squares (6 across, 4 down). How much of a whole chikki is each piece? a) A rectangle 1 square across and 2 squares down. b) A right triangle with legs 4 squares tall and 3 squares wide (half of a 3 by 4 block). c) A right triangle with legs 2 squares tall and 3 squares wide (half of a 3 by 2 block). d) A strip 1 square across and 4 squares down. e) An L-shape made of 3 squares. f) A triangle with a vertical side 4 squares long and its tip 2 squares to the right (half of a 2 by 4 block). g) A single small square. h) A right triangle with legs 2 squares tall and 1 square wide (half of a 1 by 2 block).
Book item: A paper strip is one unit long. Fold it into two equal parts and open it again. What are the lengths of the two parts created by the crease?

Book item: Now, a unit on the number line is divided into 8 equal parts. Write the fractions for the marks from 0 to 1.
Book item: On a number line, draw lines of lengths 1/10, 3/10, and 4/5.
Book item: Write five more fractions of your choice and mark them on the number line.
Book item: How many fractions lie between 0 and 1? Think, discuss with your classmates, and write your answer.
